title: Cold rebuild: the timer formatter
summary: Rebuild FormatDuration from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **FormatDuration** in *Numbers and math*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: For `seconds = 3725`, which expression gives the **minutes** part (`2`)?
steps.explain: `3725 % 3600` is `125` seconds left after the whole hour, and `125 / 60` is `2`. `seconds / 60` is `62`: it counts the hour's minutes too.

steps.title: Rebuild FormatDuration cold
prompt: Your code becomes the body of `static string FormatDuration(int seconds)`. `seconds` is given; put
`<h>h <mm>m <ss>s` in `result`, minutes and seconds padded to two digits, hours not limited to 24.
template: Dojo.Eq("one second short of a day", "23h 59m 59s", FormatDuration(86399));
steps.explain: Same tests as the original FormatDuration. It is in your memory now, not just in your Sidekick.
